title: MAX-DESIGN advanced interaction and product patterns
description: Supplementary original, searchable decision records for complex product workflows, accessibility behavior, privacy, resilient states, and measurable implementation quality.
guidance: Use these records with knowledge/design-patterns.json. They are decision aids, not automatic prescriptions. Confirm normative requirements, browser support, and project conventions before implementation.
researchBasis: WCAG 2.2 and WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide for web accessibility expectations.
MDN accessibility guidance for native semantics, keyboard use, and dynamic updates.
web.dev Core Web Vitals guidance for field-oriented performance signals.
Apple Human Interface Guidelines for platform-aware interaction and purposeful motion.

pagePatterns.title: AI conversation workspace
pagePatterns.summary: A task workspace for prompts, generated output, tool activity, revision, and recovery rather than a decorative chat transcript.
pagePatterns.question: What is the user trying to create or decide, and how can they inspect, revise, reuse, or recover the result?
priorities: Separate user input, generated output, tool activity, and system status visually and semantically.
Keep the active task and conversation context clear while longer responses arrive.
Support copy, edit, regenerate, stop, retry, and history actions only when their behavior is real.
Preserve user input when generation fails or the connection drops.
verify: Keyboard reachability of composer and message actions
Announcements that do not read every streamed token
avoid: Fake progress percentages
Claiming a tool completed when it did not
Unbounded auto-scroll that prevents reviewing earlier output

pagePatterns.title: Account and billing settings
pagePatterns.summary: A settings area for identity, plan, invoices, payment methods, security, and cancellation where consequences and status must remain unambiguous.
pagePatterns.question: Which account change is being made, when does it take effect, and how can the user verify or reverse it?
priorities: Group settings by user goal rather than internal service ownership.
Show current plan, renewal or expiry timing, billing period, and total cost before asking for confirmation.
Distinguish saved state from unsaved edits and pending server changes.
Explain cancellation, downgrade, deletion, and payment failure outcomes in plain language.
verify: Retry does not duplicate a payment action
Consequences are clear before irreversible changes
avoid: Dark patterns that hide cancellation
Fabricated urgency
Ambiguous success toasts when persistence failed

pagePatterns.title: Search-first resource catalog
pagePatterns.summary: A library or inventory interface where query, filters, sorting, and result context are the main navigation model.
pagePatterns.question: Can users express what they need, understand the current result set, and refine or clear a query without losing context?
priorities: Keep the query visible and distinguish active filters from available filters.
Show the result count and the sort order when each affects interpretation.
Make clear-all and individual filter removal easy to find.
Represent no results separately from loading, unavailable data, and an empty collection.
verify: Long filter names do not break layout
Mobile filter changes have an explicit apply or immediate-update model
avoid: Silently clearing queries after a filter change
Unlabeled icon-only filters
Showing stale counts as if they match the current query

pagePatterns.title: Data operations workspace
pagePatterns.summary: A dense work surface for reviewing records, comparing states, applying bulk actions, and investigating exceptions.
pagePatterns.question: Which records need attention, what can be changed safely, and how will users understand the scope and result of an action?
priorities: Make record identity, status, primary value, and next action scannable.
Provide selection count and scope before bulk actions.
Keep sort and filter context visible when users page or open a record.
Use explicit confirmation for high-impact bulk changes and report partial success honestly.
avoid: Ambiguous select-all scope
Color-only status
Replacing the entire table with a vague error after one row fails

interactionPatterns.title: Command palette and global search
interactionPatterns.summary: A keyboard-first launcher that lets users search destinations or actions while retaining clear focus, selection, and escape behavior.
behavior: Open through a visible control and an optional documented shortcut; never make the shortcut the only entry point.
Move through options with a predictable keyboard model and expose the active option semantically.
Enter activates the selected item; Escape closes the overlay and returns focus to the opener.
Separate actions from navigation destinations and communicate destructive or privileged actions before execution.
verify: Keyboard-only open, search, selection, and close
Screen-reader names and option count where supported
Shortcut does not intercept typing in unrelated contexts
avoid: Using a list of clickable divs without keyboard semantics
Hidden shortcut-only functionality
Executing a high-impact action on an ambiguous partial match

interactionPatterns.title: Optimistic update with rollback
interactionPatterns.summary: An interaction pattern for making low-risk changes feel immediate while keeping server truth and failure recovery explicit.
behavior: Use optimistic UI only when the action is reversible and the likely result is sufficiently predictable.
Mark pending state subtly and prevent accidental duplicate submissions where necessary.
On failure, restore the known prior value or show a clearly recoverable conflict state.
For irreversible or financial actions, prefer a confirmed request flow over speculative success.
avoid: A success message before the server confirms a consequential action
Silently reverting a change
Discarding newer user edits during rollback

interactionPatterns.title: Persistent and shareable filter state
interactionPatterns.summary: A state model for search and table controls that preserves user intent across refreshes, pagination, and shared links when appropriate.
behavior: Define which state belongs in the URL, in-session state, or saved preferences.
Keep URL query parameters canonical and validate untrusted or unsupported values.
Restore state consistently on refresh and browser navigation.
Reset pagination when a new filter makes the current page invalid.
verify: Copied URL in a second session
Filter change on a later page
avoid: Storing shareable state only in ephemeral component memory
Exposing secrets or personal data in URLs
Creating navigation history for every keystroke without an explicit policy

interactionPatterns.title: Streaming output controls
interactionPatterns.summary: Controls and feedback for incremental output that preserve perceived responsiveness without overwhelming assistive technology or the main thread.
behavior: Communicate that generation is in progress and provide a stop or cancel action when supported.
Batch visual updates when needed; do not force excessive layout or announce every token.
Distinguish partial output from completed output and make continuation or retry behavior explicit.
Respect reduced motion and avoid making attention depend solely on animation.
avoid: A fake percentage without a measurable basis
Unbounded DOM updates
Auto-scrolling that fights manual reading

densityProfiles.title: Adaptive operational density
densityProfiles.summary: A density strategy for professional tools that supports fast scanning without shrinking essential text or hiding status.
useWhen: Experienced users value scanning speed but still need readable controls
layoutRules: Use spacing rhythm and alignment to distinguish groups rather than enclosing every item in a card.
Expose a compact mode only when it has a clear benefit and stable, understandable behavior.
Keep row targets and focus indicators usable at every density setting.
On narrow screens, prioritize columns by user task or provide an explicit alternate record view.
avoid: Reducing body text simply to fit more data
Relying on hover to reveal critical fields

productProfiles.title: AI creation product
productProfiles.summary: An interface for generating, editing, and exporting content or code where trust depends on clear process states and user control.
priorities: Clear input intent and output format
Visible generation, cancellation, and failure states
Editable and exportable results
Clear distinction between generated suggestions and verified facts
risks: A model or tool failure can lose user work
Fake certainty or fake progress erodes trust
avoid: Invented model capabilities
Unverified success states
Unclear data-retention or training controls

productProfiles.title: Multi-tenant admin console
productProfiles.summary: An administration product where users operate across organizations, workspaces, projects, roles, and environments.
priorities: Keep current organization and environment visible
Explain role and access scope before a privileged action
Confirm the target and scope of bulk changes
Record outcome and partial failure clearly
risks: Cross-workspace actions can affect the wrong tenant
Permission state may change during a session
verify: Deep link to a restricted item
avoid: Ambiguous tenant switchers
Assuming a hidden role is equivalent to disabled access
Displaying confidential values to an unauthorized user

productProfiles.title: Privacy-sensitive account area
productProfiles.summary: Settings for personal data, connected services, permissions, exports, and account deletion where informed consent and recovery matter.
priorities: Use plain descriptions of data use and sharing
Request permissions at the moment of need with a clear benefit
Offer understandable export, revoke, and deletion paths
Confirm irreversible changes and explain their effects
risks: Deletion and export workflows can be legally or operationally consequential
Consent interfaces can accidentally manipulate choice
avoid: Preselected consent where it is not appropriate
Bundled unrelated permission requests
Dark patterns that obstruct refusal or cancellation

productProfiles.title: Subscription commerce
productProfiles.summary: A purchase flow where price, billing interval, renewal, trial conversion, taxes, and cancellation terms must be legible before commitment.
priorities: Show recurring total and interval near the decision point
Keep selected plan and add-ons consistent through checkout
Provide clear validation and payment recovery
Confirm the final transaction outcome from the actual service response
risks: Double submits may create duplicate orders
Locale and currency mismatch can confuse costs
avoid: False scarcity or countdowns
Hidden recurring charges
Treating a client-side click as proof of payment

styleDirections.title: Quiet layered utility
styleDirections.summary: A restrained visual system for tools where information and task completion should dominate while hierarchy still feels polished.
fitWhen: The interface is used repeatedly for work
Many content types must coexist without competing for attention
layout: Use surfaces and borders only to communicate grouping or interaction
Create hierarchy with typography, alignment, spacing, and state before adding shadows
styleDirections.colorApproach: Start from neutral surfaces and semantic roles; reserve stronger accents for actions, selected states, and meaningful status.
avoid: Uniform card grids for unrelated content
Excessive blur, gradients, glows, and shadows
Low-contrast secondary text that disappears on mobile
risks: Too little contrast can make boundaries unclear
Overly restrained design can hide affordances

colorStrategies.title: Semantic status and dark-mode roles
colorStrategies.summary: A token strategy that separates brand expression from success, warning, danger, information, focus, and selection meaning across themes.

tokens.text-primary: high-emphasis foreground for the current surface
tokens.text-muted: secondary text that still meets the applicable contrast requirement
tokens.status-success: positive completion state, paired with text or an icon
tokens.status-warning: caution state, paired with text or an icon
tokens.status-danger: error or destructive state, paired with text or an icon

verify: Test exact foreground/background pairs in each theme
Test hover, selected, disabled, and focus states
Do not encode the only meaning in hue
avoid: Using brand accent as every status
Applying identical hex values blindly across light and dark surfaces
Assuming a palette is accessible without measuring rendered pairs

motionRecipes.title: Incremental feedback motion
motionRecipes.summary: Brief motion that helps users understand a state transition or arriving content while remaining optional and non-blocking.
useWhen: A change in state benefits from spatial continuity
New content arrives incrementally and its origin matters
motionRecipes.duration: Start with short, task-sensitive transitions and verify them in context; these are design starting points, not standard-mandated timings.
implementation: Prefer opacity and transform for simple transitions when appropriate
Keep controls usable during animation
Reduce or remove nonessential movement under prefers-reduced-motion
Use text or a stable status indicator in addition to motion
avoid: Blocking an action until animation ends
Infinite decorative motion
Using animation as the only loading or success signal

uxGuidelines.title: WCAG 2.2 focus and target verification
uxGuidelines.summary: Use WCAG 2.2 as the normative reference for focus visibility, focus not obscured, and target-size requirements rather than relying on informal pixel folklore.
do: Check keyboard focus remains visible and is not fully obscured by sticky headers, dialogs, or floating controls.
Check WCAG 2.2 target-size minimum and its exceptions for applicable controls; larger targets can still be a useful usability goal.
Test the actual rendered component states and background combinations.
Use native interactive semantics where available and ensure pointer actions have keyboard equivalents.
verify: Focus near sticky edges and overlays
avoid: Claiming WCAG conformance from an automated scan alone
Treating a preferred 44px target as the exact universal WCAG 2.2 AA rule
Removing default focus indication without a better visible alternative

uxGuidelines.title: Modal dialog focus lifecycle
uxGuidelines.summary: A modal overlay must create a coherent focus lifecycle and prevent interaction with obscured background content while open.
do: Move focus into the dialog when it opens, choosing an initial target appropriate to the content and task.
Keep keyboard navigation within a modal dialog while it remains open.
Close through an explicit control and support Escape when consistent with the dialog's purpose.
Return focus to the opener or another logical location when the dialog closes.
Make background content inert to pointer and keyboard interaction while a true modal is active.
avoid: A visual overlay without modal behavior
Losing the focused element after close
Using a modal for information that could be inline

uxGuidelines.title: Combobox and autocomplete behavior
uxGuidelines.summary: Autocomplete is a keyboard interaction pattern, not merely a dropdown styled below an input.
do: Choose whether suggestions are automatic, list-like, or optional and document the behavior.
Keep DOM focus and active suggestion behavior consistent with the selected ARIA pattern.
Support arrow-key navigation and a clear acceptance/cancellation model.
Expose a useful empty-suggestions or loading status without announcing every keystroke noisily.
avoid: A custom widget that only works with a mouse
Using ARIA roles without implementing the associated keyboard model
Accepting a stale response for an older query

uxGuidelines.title: Privacy-aware authentication errors
uxGuidelines.summary: Authentication feedback should help legitimate users recover without unnecessarily revealing whether an account exists or exposing sensitive state.
do: Use an error message appropriate to the security policy and threat model.
Keep password-reset and sign-in recovery routes understandable and accessible.
Do not remove the user's non-sensitive input after a recoverable failure.
Avoid placing credentials, session tokens, or sensitive personal details in query strings or logs.
verify: Unknown account and known account paths
avoid: Leaking account existence without a deliberate risk decision
Clearing every field after a typo
Pretending the user is signed in before authentication succeeds

uxGuidelines.title: Permission request timing and choice
uxGuidelines.summary: Ask for browser, device, or connected-service permission when users understand its purpose and can still make progress where possible.
do: Explain the user-facing benefit immediately before the request.
Ask only for permissions relevant to the feature being used.
Provide a useful alternative when permission is denied, if an alternative exists.
Explain how to revisit or revoke a permission or connection.
avoid: Repeatedly prompting after refusal without a meaningful context change
Blocking unrelated tasks behind optional permissions
Making refusal visually or functionally punitive

uxGuidelines.title: Offline and degraded-network resilience
uxGuidelines.summary: Network failure is an ordinary product state that should preserve user intent and distinguish saved, pending, and unsaved work.
do: Distinguish a local draft from data confirmed by the server.
Preserve safe user input and explain whether an operation can be retried.
Use bounded retries with a clear recovery path rather than an endless spinner.
Handle duplicate submission and conflict resolution explicitly.
avoid: Showing saved before persistence is confirmed
Discarding drafts on refresh without warning
Retrying non-idempotent actions blindly

uxGuidelines.title: Status and live-announcement priority
uxGuidelines.summary: Make important async status perceivable without stealing focus or generating excessive screen-reader announcements.
do: Prefer native status semantics and appropriate live-region politeness for non-urgent updates.
Announce meaningful milestones, completion, and recoverable failure rather than every internal state mutation.
Move focus only when the user needs to act at a new location, such as a failed form submission that requires correction.
Keep visible status text synchronized with the actual operation state.
avoid: Using assertive announcements for routine changes
A spinner with no accessible context
Assuming ARIA makes a broken interaction usable

uxGuidelines.title: Empty, zero, missing, and stale data
uxGuidelines.summary: Different data conditions need different explanations so a view does not imply a false result or silently hide a system issue.
do: Distinguish a genuine numeric zero from missing, unavailable, invalid, and not-yet-loaded values.
Explain whether an empty view means no records exist or current filters match none.
Show timestamp, period, or freshness context when data can become stale.
Keep partial-data warnings close to the affected metrics.
avoid: Replacing missing values with zero without domain justification
A stale metric presented as current
A chart that implies continuous data across missing periods

uxGuidelines.title: Destructive action and recovery design
uxGuidelines.summary: High-impact actions need clear scope, proportional confirmation, a truthful outcome, and undo where feasible.
do: State what will change, which item or scope is affected, and whether it can be reversed.
Use confirmation when consequences are serious or difficult to recover from; avoid redundant confirmation for trivial actions.
Prefer undo or soft-delete when product semantics and safety allow.
Confirm completion from the actual operation and expose partial failure.
avoid: Generic confirmation text such as Are you sure?
A success toast before completion
Using confirmation as a substitute for clear initial affordances

uxGuidelines.title: Core Web Vitals and perceived performance
uxGuidelines.summary: Assess real user experience with measured loading, responsiveness, and visual stability rather than using animation smoothness as a proxy.
do: Use current Core Web Vitals definitions and published thresholds from web.dev.
Measure with the available tool and state whether evidence is field data, lab data, or a source-code inspection.
Reserve image and media dimensions, avoid unnecessary layout shifts, and load only needed code and assets.
Prioritize the slow or unstable path observed rather than applying generic optimization rituals.
avoid: Invented scores
Claiming good field performance from one local run
Optimizing a metric without checking task experience

chartPatterns.title: Time-series gaps and freshness
chartPatterns.summary: A time-series display must distinguish actual zero, absent observations, delayed ingestion, and a period that has not completed.
useWhen: Missing samples or delayed ingestion can change interpretation
implementation: Label the time range, aggregation, timezone, units, and source when these affect interpretation.
Represent missing intervals intentionally rather than automatically connecting or zero-filling them.
Show freshness or delayed-data status beside the affected display.
Keep comparisons on compatible scales and disclose any normalization.
avoid: Implying continuity through missing data
Unlabeled units
Using a truncated axis without a clear reason

chartPatterns.title: Chart summary and data alternative
chartPatterns.summary: Pair a visual chart with enough text and/or a structured data view to communicate values and trends beyond color, hover, and position.
useWhen: A chart communicates an important result
Precise values or comparisons matter to a decision
implementation: Provide a concise summary of the major trend or comparison without overstating causation.
Name axes, units, series, date range, and meaningful reference values.
Use labels, line styles, markers, or patterns when color distinctions alone are insufficient.
Offer a table or equivalent text for exact values when useful to the task.
avoid: Tooltip-only essential values
Unlabeled pie slices
Decorative animation that changes interpretation

stackGuides.title: Semantic HTML and progressive enhancement
stackGuides.summary: Use native browser behavior as the baseline and add custom interaction only where it creates meaningful value.
implementation: Prefer buttons for actions, links for navigation, native form controls for input, and headings for document structure.
Add ARIA only when native semantics do not adequately express the interaction.
Keep essential content and navigation available when nonessential scripts or effects fail.
Avoid positive tabindex values and custom widgets without a documented keyboard model.
avoid: Clickable divs where a button or link fits
ARIA attributes used as a substitute for interaction behavior
Custom control design without corresponding state logic

stackGuides.title: Performance evidence and reporting
stackGuides.summary: Separate code-level optimization hypotheses from measured user-facing results and state the scope of every performance claim.
implementation: Inspect bundle cost, image dimensions, font behavior, long tasks, layout shifts, and repeated renders when relevant.
Record device, route, network conditions, test method, and whether metrics are lab or field evidence.
Use comparable conditions when reporting a before/after improvement.
Keep performance verification separate from usability and accessibility claims.
avoid: Claiming a universal improvement from one test
Reporting undocumented timings
Optimizing a benchmark while breaking accessibility or product clarity
